topbar: For UK IT services firms with {THRESHOLD}+ turnover

h1: More of the right sales conversations.
We are paid when a deal closes.
hero.lede: We fill your sales team's calendar with meetings that fit your best clients. You keep the ad accounts and the data. We invoice only on deals that close.
hero.cta: See whether we would take you on
hero.micro: A few questions, about three minutes. We turn most firms down, and would rather say so now than in a meeting.

works: You run a UK IT services firm turning over **{THRESHOLD}** or more
You sell projects or contracts where one new client is worth **£25,000** or more in the first year
Your own sales team takes the meetings, and can respond within **two working days**
You have capacity to take on new clients now
not: You are below **{THRESHOLD}** turnover or have been trading for less than **two years**
You sell products or software licences rather than services
You are at capacity, in which case come back when you are not
You want leads without a sales team to follow them up
fit.footnote: Turnover is checked against public records after you apply.

paid.h2: We are paid when a deal closes.
paid.p1: No retainer, no setup fee, no minimum term. We invoice a commission on deals that close from campaigns we run. If nothing closes, there is nothing to invoice. The advertising budget is separate. You pay it directly to the platforms, from your own accounts.
paid.p2: The commission depends on what a client is worth to you, so we agree it before anything runs. It is not published, because it is not the same for two firms.

keep.h2: Your accounts. Your data. Your sales team.

items.title: The ad accounts are yours
items.text: Campaigns run in ad accounts you own. You pay the platforms directly, with no markup from us.

items.title: The data is yours
items.text: Leads, results and sales are tracked in your own CRM. If we stop working together, you keep all of it.

items.title: Your team takes the meetings
items.text: We do not replace your sales team. We fill their calendar with conversations that fit.

meeting.lede: We do not pitch. We sit down with your numbers and work out what it would take to reach next year's target.

steps.title: Before the call
steps.text: You tell us your turnover, your target for next year, and what a typical new client is worth.

steps.title: On the call
steps.text: We confirm four numbers together: last year's turnover, next year's target, what a new client is worth in year one, and how many sales meetings turn into clients.

steps.title: Within 24 hours
steps.text: You receive a one page sheet with the arithmetic: new clients per month needed, sales meetings per month that requires, and how that compares with your pipeline today.

meeting.notice: You keep the sheet whether or not we work together. It contains your numbers only. No quote, no commission rate, no promise.

clients.footnote: Named with each client's written permission.

items.q: How is this different from an agency on a retainer?
items.a: A retainer is paid whether or not anything closes. Our invoice depends on a deal closing, so we only earn when your sales team does.
You do. We work inside them. If we stop, they stay with you.
You do, directly to the platforms and from ad accounts you own. We add no markup. Our commission is a separate matter and is only invoiced when a deal closes.

items.q: What do you need from us to start?
items.a: Access to your ad accounts, your CRM, and about an hour with whoever runs sales. Your sales team needs to be able to follow up within two working days.

items.q: Why do you ask for turnover?
items.a: Because the arithmetic only works above a certain size. We would rather say no early than start something neither of us can make pay.
No. We can show you the arithmetic and the method. We cannot promise a number of meetings or deals.

items.q: What if we want to stop?
items.a: There is no minimum term. You stop, and you keep the accounts and the data.

questions.title: What is your main area of IT services?
Roughly what did the business turn over in the last financial year?
How many people work in the business?
What does the business spend on marketing in a typical month, all channels?
What is a typical new client worth to you in the first year?
How long does a typical sale take, from first meeting to signed?
What turnover are you aiming for next year?
questions.hint: Optional. It helps us prepare for the call.

questions.title: Who would decide whether to work with us?
options: Me, with a co-founder or board
Someone else, I would bring them in

questions.title: How many new clients could you take on in the next three months?

book.h1: Thank you. Choose a time that suits you.
book.text: Pick a slot for a {OFFER}. Your own numbers are all we need.

takk.text: We will send a confirmation and a short note on what to have to hand: last year's turnover, next year's target, and what a typical new client is worth.

review.h1: Thank you. We will be in touch within one working day.
review.text: We want to check a few things before we suggest a time.

not-now.h1: Thank you. Come back when you have capacity.
not-now.text: If you are at capacity now, we will ask again in three months.

not-a-fit.h1: Thank you. This is not the right fit at the moment.
not-a-fit.text: We work with UK IT services firms above a certain size. If that changes, we would be glad to hear from you.
